title: Synthesis, Crystal Structure, and Modelling of a New Tetramer Complex of Europium

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: tetrakis(europium) nonakis(ethyl 4,4,4-trifluoroacetoacetate) tris(μ3-hydroxido) triaqua ethyl acetate solvate

synthesis.procedure: ETA and europium chloride were used as received. [Eu4(η3-ETA)3(η2-ETA)6(μ3-OH)3(H2O)3] was prepared by dissolving 2 mmol of europium chloride in triethylorthoformate, then drying it and dissolving it in anhydrous THF. Ethyl 4,4,4-trifluoroacetoacetate, previously deprotonated with strong alkali in dried THF under an inert atmosphere, was added. The compound was dried, neutralized with NH4Cl, filtered, and washed with water and solvent to remove excess lanthanide chloride and ligand. The solid was dried under vacuum over silica in a desiccator. Single crystals of the ethyl acetate solvate were grown from cyclohexane/ethyl acetate at room temperature over 5 days.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: inert-atmosphere solution synthesis in dried THF; vacuum drying over silica; crystallization from cyclohexane/ethyl acetate
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Dried, neutralized with NH4Cl, filtered, washed with water and solvent, and dried under vacuum over silica. Single crystals grown from cyclohexane/ethyl acetate at room temperature over 5 days.

properties.summary: The Eu4 tetramer is luminescent, showing characteristic 5D0→7FJ (J=0–4) emission at 77 K with four 5D0→7F0 peaks (17226, 17238, 17247, 17256 cm−1) consistent with four distinct Eu3+ sites. The 298 K excitation spectrum (monitored at 612 nm) contains a broad ligand-related band at 357 nm overlapping 4f–4f lines. Experimental Judd–Ofelt intensity parameters from the 77 K emission spectrum are Ω2=11.14×10−20 cm2 and Ω4=6.40×10−20 cm2, with spontaneous emission coefficients A02=336.0 s−1 and A04=81.60 s−1; theory indicates dynamic-coupling dominance. UV–vis absorption of the ETA n→π* bands was also reported. Quantum-yield measurements were planned but not reported.
